sentences.text:
Bench: K. Lakshman
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice K. Lakshman
 Writ Petition No.17712 Of 2024
Oral Order

: 
Heard Sri T.S.Praveen Kumar, learned counsel, representing Ms. Manjiri S Ganu, learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Revenue appearing for respondent Nos.1 to 3 and Smt. B. Geetha, learned Standing Counsel for National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) appearing for respondent Nos.4 and 5.
Perused the record.

2. Petitioner is claiming that it is the absolute owner and possessor of land admeasuring Acs.6.21gts., in Sy.No.100 (part), Acs.7.35 gts., in Sy.No.101 (part), Ac.1.38 gts., in Sy.No.112 (part)
and Acs.2.26 gts., in Sy.No.113 (part) situated at Thimmapur Village, Kothur Mandal, Shadnagar presently in Ranga Reddy District, under a registered sale deed bearing document No.2005 of 1987,
dated 26.08.1987.
According to the petitioner, it KL,J W.P.No.17712 of 2024 has constructed compound wall encircling the said area.
It has also constructed factory and it is running the said unit.

In proof of the same, petitioner has filed a copy of the said sale deed and proceedings, dated 11.07.1991, 23.07.1991, 28.04.1988 and 24.11.2022.
3.

While the matter stood thus, respondent No.5 has issued a notice, dated 12.06.2024 stating that there is a proposal for extension of 6 laning of existing 4 lane from Km 22.300 (Thondupally) to Km34.144 (Kothur) (Design Length 11.844km) on Hyderabad to Bangalore Section of NH-44 in the State of Telangana.
Vide his letter, dated 19.04.2024, respondent No.3 submitted the survey report giving extent of land getting affected for the said project.
The land in Sy.Nos.100 and 101/2 of Thimmapur Village of the Kothur Mandal is not getting affected as per the said survey report.
However, compound wall and fencing has been erected beyond the survey line and same comes under encroachment.
Valuation of compound wall and KL,J fencing has been carried out by the R&B Department and same shall be compensated.
Therefore, respondent No.5 requested the petitioner to provide bank details to arrange for compensation for affected compound wall and fencing.

Further, it is requested to make arrangement to shift the compound wall and fencing as per markings already done at the site by 24.06.2024, failing which demolition of compound wall shall be done by this office through EPC Contractor.
4. Challenging the said notice, petitioner filed the present writ petition.

sentences.text: 5. Vide order, dated 09.07.2024, this Court directed both the parties to maintain status quo considering that in similar circumstances in respect of adjacent land of the subject property, this Court granted interim order, dated 16.04.2024 in W.P.No.34663 of 2023.
KL,J 6.
Learned counsel for the petitioner would contend that the petitioner never encroached into any land.
It has constructed compound wall, fencing and encircling the aforesaid subject property.
Even then, respondent No.5 has issued the said notice, dated 12.06.2024.

Therefore, the said notice,
dated 12.06.2024 is in violation of the principles of natural justice and procedure laid down under the National Highways Authority of India Act, 1988 (for short 'the Act, 1988).

entities.text: National Highways Authority of India Act, 1988
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: They cannot demolish the compound wall without following due procedure laid down under law.
Even in the list of encroachments filed by respondent Nos.4 and 5, the name of the petitioner is not there.
According to them, the subject compound wall is in Sy.No.26 of Thimmapur Village.
Therefore, the entire action of respondent Nos.4 and 5 is illegal.

7. Whereas, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition and Smt. B. Geetha,
learned Standing Counsel appearing for respondent Nos.4 and 5 submits KL,J that the subject property is in Sy.No.26, petitioner constructed compound wall encroaching into the National Highway.

However, they will conduct survey and demarcate the subject property belongs to the petitioner and land in Sy.No.26 of Thimmapur Village strictly in accordance with law and then they will take action.
If the subject property of the petitioner is required for road widening, they will follow due procedure laid down under law and pay compensation, if necessary.
8. The aforesaid facts would reveal that the petitioner is claiming that it is the absolute owner and possessor of land in Sy.Nos.100 (part), 101 (part) 112 (part) and 113 (part).

According to respondent Nos.2 to 5, petitioner has constructed compound wall by encroaching into land in Sy.No.26 i.e.,
Highway.
Thus, there is a dispute with regard to the identification of the property.
9. As discussed supra, at the cost of repetition, according to the petitioner, the subject land is in KL,J Sy.Nos100 and 101 of Thimmapur Village.
According to respondent Nos.2 to 5, the subject land is in Sy.No.26.

In the light of the same, this Court is of the considered view that respondent No.3 has to conduct survey, afresh strictly in accordance with law to resolve the said issue for identification of the aforesaid property belongs to the petitioner and land in Sy.No.26 of Thimmapur Village.

10. Referring to the agreement, learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition and learned Standing Counsel appearing for respondent Nos.4 and 5 would submit that they will complete the survey within ten (10) days from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.

11. It is relevant to note that vide order, dated 01.10.2024, this Court disposed of the writ petition vide W.P.No.34663 of 2023 considering the fact that they have already paid compensation for the portion which are falling under acquisition and so far as illegal and unauthorized constructions are concerned, the KL,J respondents are following the due procedure in accordance with the WALTA Act and that respondents were directed to follow due procedure laid down under law, if the houses Hil Ltd. 12. In the light of the said submissions, this Writ Petition is disposed of directing respondent Nos.2 to 5 to conduct survey with the help of Mandal Surveyor of respondent No.3, demarcate the aforesaid land belongs to the petitioner and land in Sy.No.26 of Thimmapur Village by putting the petitioner, all affected parties on notice and affording them an opportunity.

On conclusion of survey,
the aforesaid land of the petitioner is affected, they will pay compensation to the petitioner in terms of the Act, 1988.
However, they will complete the survey within ten (10) days from today.

Thereafter,
they shall pay compensation to the affected area, if any, within a KL,J period of four (4) weeks thereafter.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel thereto, miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in the Writ Petition shall stand closed.
K. LAKSHMAN, J March 06, 2025 ssm Hil Ltd.
